correctness.rationale: Proof identifies complete nonalgebraic one-types with ideal/filter pairs satisfying L<U; excludes only comparability-generating profiles. For cover-tree P, directed lower/upper principal subtrees give D_v and U_v product recursions. Each nonempty upper filter has an antichain of minimal elements. If that antichain has one minimum v, nonempty compatible ideals number D_v-2. With at least two minima and a lower witness, unique undirected paths yield a unique greatest common lower bound v and at least two upper-cover branches; the number of such filters is U_v-2-sum_{v<.w}(U_w-1), and compatible nonempty ideals number D_v-1. The baseline L-empty or U-empty is 2J(P)-1. The cases are disjoint and exhaustive. A separate two-state ideal DP on the undirected cover tree computes J(P), so all terms use linear many O(n)-bit integer operations. Standalone direct reachability-based enumeration matched 43,614 exhaustive labeled directed trees through six vertices and 480 larger reproducible samples. A finite check is only corroboration; no proof for cover graphs containing cycles is given.

Existing height-two general bipartite formula and hardness theorem do not cover arbitrary-height oriented cover trees; general hardness does not preclude a restricted efficient algorithm.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither previously identified tractable subclass contains all tree-cover orders. The N-shaped four-element cover-tree witness separates the new domain from N-free/series-parallel families; adjoining arbitrarily many incomparable lower arms gives unbounded width. General unrestricted hardness and count of linear extensions do not imply or subsume the claimed specialized formula.

originality.rationale: Closest accessible results count unrestricted random-poset 1-types via ideal/filter pairs and prove general hardness, or handle rooted forests and N-free series-parallel posets; none states the directed-cover-tree formula. The four-element N-poset is itself a cover tree but not series-parallel, separating the all-orientations claim from the strongest nearby special-case recurrences. Jochemko concerns order maps, Felsner-Manneville concerns linear extensions, and Pretzel 1980 concerns insertion-position structures (abstract only). Actual semantic-index and literature comparisons did not find coverage, but absence of a match is not proof of worldwide priority. Pretzel full text and published full unrestricted-type article were inaccessible and remain residual risks.

value.rationale: This gives an exact linear-arithmetic counting theorem for a natural and substantially broader restricted family than rooted forests or series-parallel orders; its width can grow without bound and it includes the forbidden N configuration. The branching-point lemma and two opposite recurrences are a structural reason for tractability despite general #P-completeness. It yields reproducible exact counts for all sizes, not a small arbitrary table or a mere restatement of a basic ideal-count recurrence.
